bull_case: MELI has a long runway across commerce, fintech, credit, ads and logistics, with engagement evidence showing that recent investment is changing customer behavior and deepening the ecosystem.
bear_case: Current reinvestment is consuming owner cash faster than it is producing incremental profit. Credit-card economics are negative and H1 operating income fell despite 49% revenue growth.
thesis: RF is the binding weakness. MELI has a genuine long reinvestment runway, but current-cycle incremental returns are not yet good enough to call 'excellent.' TTM reinvestment absorption is about 29%, mapping to runway 70. TTM adjusted FCF is roughly $1.13B, or about $22/share, down from about $29/share in FY2025 despite flat shares. Until cash conversion and credit-card economics recover, Compounder-level RF is not demonstrated.

evidence.claim: Using FY2025 plus H1 2026 less H1 2025, TTM CFO is about $13.905B, capex $1.496B and product/technology expense $2.579B; (capex + product/tech)/CFO is about 29.3%.
TTM adjusted FCF is approximately $1.127B = FY2025 $1.481B + H1 2026 $158M - H1 2025 $512M, about $22.2/share versus roughly $29.2/share in FY2025.
H1 2026 revenue grew 49.4% and gross profit 36.8%, yet operating income fell from $1.588B to $1.294B as provisions, marketing and product investment rose.
Recent commerce investments improved conversion, retention, category breadth and ecosystemic-user growth, providing evidence of future value even though current cash returns are weak.
Credit-card NIMAL was -2.5% in Q2 2026 while the credit portfolio exceeded $16B, so a large current reinvestment pool is not yet earning clearly attractive risk-adjusted returns.

counterevidence: FY2025 adjusted FCF grew to $1.481B from $1.215B in 2024, so current compression follows a period of improving owner cash flow.
Recent free-shipping cohorts have higher retention and engagement, indicating some current spending is productive growth investment.
Share count is essentially flat, so successful reinvestment accrues to existing owners.
Ads and payments are scaling higher-margin monetization on the existing ecosystem.
unknowns: Full-cycle risk-adjusted ROIC of credit cards.
Payback period on the latest logistics/free-shipping investments.
Normalized adjusted-FCF margin after the 2026 investment wave.
falsifiers: TTM adjusted FCF/share fails to recover through 2027-2028.
Credit-card NIMAL remains below breakeven while the portfolio keeps scaling.
Logistics/marketing investment remains elevated without sustained cohort retention and share gains.

hard_veto_flags.rationale: Current returns are weaker, but engagement gains, gross-profit growth and prior FCF improvement do not establish a structural collapse below capital cost.
Diluted shares are essentially flat/slightly lower YoY; reinvestment is not being funded through material equity dilution.

key_kpis.name: TTM adjusted FCF/share
key_kpis.threshold: recover above FY2025 ~$29/share before treating RF as Compounder quality

key_kpis.name: Incremental operating profit vs growth spend
key_kpis.threshold: operating-profit growth resumes while engagement remains strong

subscores.rationale: Recent investment is clearly producing usage and gross-profit growth, but operating income and adjusted FCF have deteriorated and credit-card NIMAL is negative. Returns are promising but not yet 'excellent'.
TTM internal reinvestment absorption is about 29.3%. Under the locked band-centre interpolation this rounds to 70, while multiple regional value pools support a long runway.
TTM adjusted FCF/share is roughly 24% below FY2025 despite flat shares. The decline is partly intentional growth investment, so 40 recognizes both real compression and normalization potential.

uncertainties.rationale: Current investment cohorts have not seasoned enough to establish full-cycle risk-adjusted returns.
The breadth and duration of potential reinvestment paths are well evidenced.
Credit and customer-fund mechanics make cash conversion volatile, but adjusted FCF explicitly attempts to remove those distortions and is still down.

dilution_metrics.rationale: Shares are flat; the current per-share weakness comes from cash conversion, not dilution.
